name: Commercial and office cleaning

pf.license.need: Usually none for office cleaning and floor care. Where the state's or city's rules require a business license or registration for janitorial work, the form asks for it. Work at height (outside windows above the ground floor), pest control, mold, asbestos and biohazard cleanup are separate licensed or certified trades in some places and are not offered here.
pf.license.ask: The company's business registration or local business license number, where the form asks for one.
pf.license.who_holds: The business. Crew members need no license of their own unless the state's form says so.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks_live: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.insurance_bond: General liability, workers' comp and a janitorial bond are common, and a building often asks for a certificate of insurance. 'Insured' or 'bonded' is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
pf.license.background_checks: Crew members who hold keys or codes: the business's own word that they are checked, or a check Rosie holds where the state's rules require one. It is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
pf.license.not_this_work: Pest control, mold removal over the state's size cutoff, asbestos, biohazard or crime-scene cleanup, and window work above the ground floor are licensed or certified in some places. They aren't office cleaning. Home cleaning is a different business.

pf.services.pattern: Set service: a fixed service at the customer's place, often repeating, priced by the space's size.

list.price_kind: set by the customer's answers (square feet, restrooms, floors)
list.example: up to 1,500 sq ft, 2 restrooms: $179 (the example business's own price)

list.where: at the customer's place (an office, shop or studio)
list.money: card saved at booking for the late-cancel and lockout fee, or nothing taken; Rosie texts the bill after the clean

list.example: once a week: $135 a visit; twice a week and every 2 weeks are priced by the same answers
list.length: about 2 hours for a crew of two
list.where: at the customer's place; nobody needs to be there
list.money: card saved or nothing taken; the bill is texted after each visit

list.name: Floor strip and wax
list.price_kind: set by square feet and floor type
list.example: $150 for a small suite (up to 500 sq ft)
list.length: about 4 hours; the floor needs hours to dry before foot traffic
list.where: at the customer's place, a closed area
list.money: a deposit, where the state's caps allow ($40 in the example); the rest is billed after the work

list.name: Carpet cleaning
list.example: $199 for a suite up to 1,000 sq ft (hot-water extraction)
list.length: about 3 hours; carpet needs hours to dry
list.money: card saved or nothing taken; billed after

list.price_kind: quoted from the customer's photos first
list.example: $640 for a small suite after a remodel

list.money: a deposit where the state's caps allow ($160 in the example); the rest is billed after

pf.services.capacity: A clean takes a crew of two: a lead and a helper. A mat drop-off needs one person at the counter.
pf.services.nobody_home: Yes, for most plan visits: entry by key, fob, door code or lockbox the business holds. DONE with after photos confirms it. The first visit and any floor care have the on-site contact reachable by phone.
pf.services.not_offered: Home cleaning, pest control, mold over the state's size cutoff, sewage, biohazards, window work above the ground floor, cleaning inside server rooms, vaults or cash areas.
pf.services.drop_off_slots: Mats, mop heads and cloths are booked into drop-off slots by the shop's daily number, with no washer named; the items go to a mat washer with the skill once they're in.

pf.questions.who_may_book: The owner, a manager or the office manager of the business that is cleaned, or the property manager of the building. A tenant who doesn't control a shared area needs the property manager's OK for it.

words: biohazards: blood, body fluids, needles, a crime or trauma scene
a mold patch over the state's size cutoff
floors, stairs or ladders that aren't safe
what_happens: A gas smell, smoke or fire: leave and call 911. Rosie never places the call. No booking until it's safe.

Sewage, biohazards, an unknown spill, asbestos or lead dust, or mold over the cutoff: Rosie says a cleaner can't take that on and points to a specialist. The rest of the space can still be booked with that area left out.
Sewage: keep people out of the area, and stay out if the water is near outlets.
Sparking or exposed wiring, or an unsafe floor: stay out of the area; no booking for it until it's fixed.
Bedbugs or rodents: pest control comes first; the clean is booked after.
Home cleaning isn't this business: no booking, and the AI can look for a home cleaning company.
pf.safety.booking_goes_on: Yes, with the area left out (sewage, biohazards, a spill, mold, wiring, a floor). No, for a gas smell, smoke or fire. Pest problems wait for pest control.

pf.first_steps.first_clean: A new account's first clean is an initial clean (deeper than the weekly clean), unless a pro cleaned the space in the last 30 days.
pf.first_steps.plan: A plan starts after the first clean. Cancelling the first clean also ends the plan that starts after it, and the customer is told first.
pf.first_steps.photos: A post-construction clean is priced from the customer's photos first. A large space is walked through before it is priced.
prep_for_reminder: Clear desks and floors of loose items
Lock away cash, keys and papers you don't want touched
Leave the entry code on the secure page, not in a text
Tell the building if the crew needs a sign-in
pf.first_steps.floor_test: Floor strip and wax: a spot test of the finish on a hidden corner first. Carpet cleaning: a color test on a hidden corner. Custom logo mats at the shop: a short color test first, so the logo won't bleed in the wash (the example: 15 minutes, at least 2 days before; it stays good for 3 months).

pf.visit.check_in: Someone there: the code at the door, entered by the crew lead. Nobody there (most plan visits): no code; the lead opens the door with the key, fob or code the business gave.
pf.visit.entry_codes: Shown only to the crew lead, only on the visit day, and each opening is logged. The key goes back where the business keeps it at the end. The alarm is set again when the crew leaves.
pf.visit.lockout: No way in when nobody needs to be there (a key, fob or code fails, or the alarm won't clear): the crew lead texts it, Alex gets a link for a new code, and the crew waits 30 minutes, then leaves. A lockout fee only if the owner confirms it.
pf.visit.drop_off: At the business (Lee Mat Care): the code is given at the counter when the items are left. Status words IN, DRYING, READY. READY comes with a photo. Pick-up only by the customer or someone they name.
pf.visit.changes_at_visit: Add-ons only when the on-site contact asks, priced before they're done. A large space clean is priced before any work. A right to cancel only where the state's rules give one.
pf.visit.proof_done: Before photos of each area, an area-by-area checklist, after photos from the same angles. DONE with after photos when nobody's there. Photos never show screens, papers, people or private offices.
pf.visit.breakage: Reported with photos the same day; the owner decides how to make it right.

pf.money.start: Office cleaning: a card saved at booking for the late-cancel and lockout fee, or nothing taken; Rosie texts the bill after each clean. Floor care and post-construction cleans: a deposit where the state's caps allow. Mat drop-offs: nothing taken, paid at the counter at pick-up.
pf.money.deposits: None by default. Sam can set a deposit or the full price per service, within the state's caps (the example: $40 on a $150 floor strip and wax, $160 on a $640 post-construction clean). Deposit cap: from the state form.
pf.money.fees: Late cancel and lockout: the business's own fee (the example: $89), never more than what was paid now when money was paid now. Needs a saved card. The owner confirms each one; no answer, no fee. No card saved, no fee.
pf.money.plans: Each plan visit is billed after its own clean. Where the owner turns it on, one bill a month covers all of a plan's visits, with a line for each. A plan charges the saved card only if the owner sets it and the customer said yes to those terms first. Rosfield's $2 counts once a month for a plan.
pf.money.tips: None by default; offices rarely tip.
pf.money.tax: A sales tax line only where the state taxes janitorial work, from the state form.

never_in_texts: Entry, fob, lockbox, door, garage and alarm codes
Health reasons, like an allergy behind a product to avoid
pf.messages.photos: Photos of the space go only to the customer and the business. Crews don't photograph screens, papers, people or private offices.
pf.messages.languages: English and Spanish. The crew's language shows on the job.

skills: Office, restroom and break room cleaning
Floor care: strip, wax and buffing
Mat, mop head and cloth washing, stain treatment, custom logo mats
pf.staff.crews: Two per site: a lead, who holds the entry code and texts DONE, and a helper. A person who works alone at a site adds an emergency contact, and a missed safety check gives that contact the job's address only.
pf.staff.licenses: None per person unless the state's form says so.
pf.staff.new_person_ok: A cleaner the customer hasn't booked is offered by text first, never sent without an OK. No answer: the rest of the booked crew comes and the clean takes about an hour longer, or it moves with no fee.
pf.staff.who_oks: The owner OKs quotes over the limit. The office manager may too; the owner's answer wins.

plans: The plan's terms show before any card is asked: how often, the price a visit, when it's billed, that it runs until ended, and how to end it.
The plan gets its own yes, apart from the booking, and the terms are texted back.
A price change is told 30 days ahead, or more where the state's rules ask.
Any reminder the state's rules require for a running plan.
pf.rules.add_on_at_home: A right to cancel only where the state's rules give one for work sold at the customer's place.
pf.rules.written_contract: Above an amount or a term, where the state's rules require it. The scope (areas, days, who supplies paper and soap) shows in the plan's terms.
pf.rules.landlord: Common areas and shared restrooms belong to the building: the property manager's OK is needed when the tenant doesn't control them.
pf.rules.records: 7 years, with the before and after photos.

matter_most: Lockout: a key, fob or code that fails, or an alarm that won't clear, when nobody needs to be there. The crew waits 30 minutes, then leaves; the owner decides any fee.
Something breaks during the clean: photos the same day; the owner decides.
Missed spots: tell the business within 24 hours; a free re-clean of those areas within 48 hours. A redo, never money from Rosie.
A crew member is out: a new person is offered first; no answer, the rest of the crew comes for longer.
Skip, pause or end a plan, and a plan's price change.
Sewage, a spill, biohazards or mold found during the clean: that area stops; a written note goes to the customer.
A door the crew has no key for, or an area the customer locked: it is skipped and noted, never forced.
Waxed or wet floors: the area is closed until dry; the customer is told how long.
A holiday or a building closure: Sam keeps the visit or moves it, with no fee.
Mats or cloths not picked up: reminders; after the free days, a storage fee only if the owner starts it, after written notice.
Several open bookings (a plan's next visits): which one is asked first.
pf.edges.rest: All other edge cases are handled the generic way.

notes:
Pilot: cleaner (from), refitted Oct 27. Commercial cleaning runs like a set service: a crew at the customer's space, often nobody there, on a plan that repeats, billed after each visit. The cleaner's shape fits; what it lacks is added: a business customer (an office, shop or studio, not a home), keys, fobs, door and alarm codes held by the crew lead, areas to skip, floor care, carpet cleaning, post-construction cleans priced from photos, large spaces priced at a walkthrough, and a free walkthrough.
Flow B is the usual side: Lee Office Care (office cleaning, plus floor care as its second kind of work). Flow A is the less usual side: Lee Mat Care, Sam's second company, where a business drops off entrance mats, mop heads and cloth bundles and picks them up washed (the cleaner's rug drop-off, re-themed). Mat care is done at the shop only: the both-places and other-place branches are off in both flows.
Money (B): main list|card|bill (card saved for the $89 late-cancel and lockout fee; Rosie texts the bill after each clean). Also list|none|bill, list|deposit|bill (floor strip and wax $150: $40 now, $110 on the bill, fee $40), photos|deposit|bill (post-construction clean $640: $160 now, $480 on the bill), visit|card|bill (large space clean priced at the walkthrough). Money (A): list|none|counter (main), list|card|counter, list|full|none, photos|none|counter, visit|none|counter. A fee is never more than what was paid now. An added service is paid at the visit or on the bill. Nothing is charged without a yes.
Offices are billed after the work, so no path charges the saved card at DONE. The sign-up money card (S1-13) keeps the master's example reply (some services paid in full); it is an example, the owner decides.
Never sent now: cleaning is booked ahead. S2-30 branch 1 is off and the booking choices are limited (B: a set time in a window; A: a set start); the rows and lines that said 'takes jobs sent now' (S2-30, S1-21) are re-worded.
Plan: weekly (a plan can also be twice a week or every 2 weeks), $135 a visit, its own yes, terms texted back (B6-x01, B6-x02). The first plan visit is Thu Oct 29, a week after the initial clean on Thu Oct 22.
Own steps: B6-x01 and B6-x02 (plan terms texted back; the date runs forward from the first clean).
No tips fact (offices rarely tip); no stages, documents or video facts. Facts: plans, firststeps, dropoff, photos, extrawork, monthlybill (a business account can get one bill a month for a plan, if the owner turns it on). Switches: none (cancelright off: add-ons are done at the visit). Settings: arrive A setstart / B window; cutoff A 24 hours before, B 2 days before.
Licenses: janitorial and floor care need none in most places; the form asks where the state or city requires a registration. Pest control, mold removal over the cutoff, asbestos, biohazard cleanup and window work above the ground floor are not offered. Certificate of insurance and crew background checks show as checked only when Rosie holds the paper.
Safety words (pf.safety): a gas smell, smoke or fire (911, no booking); sewage, biohazards, an unknown spill, asbestos or lead dust, mold over the cutoff (that area left out, a specialist); sparking wires or an unsafe floor (stay out); bedbugs or rodents (pest control first). The danger examples in B3-11 and B3-18 use sewage; everyday examples use none of these words.
Names: crew leads Imani and Felix (flow B), mat washers Tomas and Hana (flow A). Addresses: 210 Harbor St (the office), 48 Dock St (the mat shop), 700 Bay St (the office's travel area). Registration numbers use the REG-0451 format. The example times (8 to 10am windows) are the master's; Sam sets the real hours.
Kept words: 'leak' (the privacy leak in the shared rules), 'color' (the color test for logo mats), 'visit fee' (the master's own words for a fee owed after a no to a price).
